clue.text: Race the old lady runs with floppy hat on

indicators.note: 'with' joins the floppy letters to what comes before them, keeping them alongside

parts.note: 'the old lady' is slang for one's mother, MA
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

indicators.note: something floppy hangs loose and out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Mum jogs a long race wearing a sagging sun hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the old lady' is British slang for one's mother; 'runs' is the cricket scoring abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-distance running event of about twenty-six miles is a classic race.

clue.text: Difficulty encountered in powerful vessel

parts.note: a hard blow is a powerful one
a ship is a sea-going vessel

explanation.surface: Trouble met aboard a mighty ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Hardship is suffering or adversity, a synonym for difficulty in life.

clue.text: Grab small part

definitions.meaning: a brief fragment, as of a song or conversation overheard

explanation.surface: Seize a little piece.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to seize suddenly and a short fragment, as in a few bars of melody.

clue.text: Untidy writing produced by son on edge

indicators.note: in a down clue 'on' puts the first piece above the second

parts.note: to edge forward is to crawl, moving slowly

explanation.surface: A nervous boy's messy handwriting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'edge' reads as nervousness, but it is a verb meaning to inch along.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrawl is careless, hard-to-read handwriting.

clue.text: Good-natured tolerance of coppers going round at one

indicators.note: the coins encircle the next pieces, which sit inside them

parts.note: copper coins are pence
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Police patiently circling around a single suspect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coppers' suggests police, but means copper coins.
explanation.definitionFit: Patience is calm, uncomplaining forbearance of others.

clue.text: Careless, extremely rude young lady

indicators.note: taking only the extremes, the outermost letters, of the word rude

parts.note: a miss is a young unmarried woman

explanation.surface: A rude, thoughtless girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Remiss means negligent, failing in one's duty.

clue.text: British, in a spot, don't vote

indicators.note: the abbreviation goes inside the phrase 'a stain'

parts.note: a stain is a spot or mark

explanation.surface: A Briton in a tight spot refuses to vote.
explanation.definitionFit: To abstain is to decline to cast a ballot.

clue.text: Tobacco tin open

parts.note: Sn is the chemical symbol for tin
a flower that is out is open

explanation.surface: Opening a tobacco tin.
explanation.definitionFit: Snout is British prison slang for tobacco, a crossword-favourite sense.

clue.text: The acre? Wrong: you need a bigger measure of land

indicators.note: the phrase is set wrong, its letters put in another order

explanation.surface: A pedant insists the acre is too small and a larger land unit is required.
explanation.definitionFit: A hectare is 10,000 square metres, about two and a half acres.

clue.text: Partner, hot on American group

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps
a band is a musical group

explanation.surface: A sexy partner who is a fan of a US band.
explanation.definitionFit: A husband is a married partner.

clue.text: Keen to press old skirt

indicators.note: the keen word squeezes the next letter into its middle

parts.note: avid means keen or eager

explanation.surface: Someone eager to iron a vintage skirt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skirt' is a verb here, not clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: To skirt an issue is to go round it and evade it.

clue.text: Conductor of opera, name in Italy

parts.note: Tosca is Puccini's opera
taken as written
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: A conductor of opera making a name for himself in Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Arturo Toscanini was a celebrated Italian orchestral conductor.

clue.text: Punishment given after assault: article by school principal became prominent in the news

indicators.note: the punishment comes after all the other pieces

parts.note: to hit is to strike or assault
the is the definite article
a head teacher runs a school
lines are a written school punishment, copying a sentence many times

explanation.surface: A school story: a pupil punished after attacking a teacher and then made the news.
explanation.walkthrough: LINES is a British school punishment: writing out the same sentence repeatedly.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for appearing as a major story in the press.

clue.text: Personal assistant brought in important item of stationery

indicators.note: the assistant's letters are placed inside the word for important

parts.note: noted means eminent or important

explanation.surface: An office PA hired as a key part of the stationery cupboard.
explanation.definitionFit: A notepad is a pad of paper for jotting things down.

clue.text: Still coming over to cover separate social event

indicators.note: the reversed word wraps around the next piece
in a down clue the word comes over, read upwards and so backwards

parts.note: yet means still, as in 'not done yet'
apart means separate

explanation.surface: Someone still coming round to cover for a separated couple at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming over' turns YET into TEY, which then holds APART.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea party is an afternoon social gathering with tea and cakes.

clue.text: Republican vacating flat, and unpleasant house

indicators.note: the Republican moves out of the word for flat, leaving it

parts.note: dry wine, or dry humour, is flat
nasty means unpleasant

explanation.surface: A Republican moving out of a flat and into a horrible house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vacating' removes R from DRY, leaving DY.
explanation.definitionFit: A house in the sense of a ruling family line, such as the House of Windsor.

clue.text: Nobleman's wife expected short game

indicators.note: cut short, the word loses its last letter

parts.note: due means expected, as a train due at noon
chess is a board game

explanation.surface: A noblewoman who wants a quick game.
explanation.definitionFit: A duchess is the wife of a duke.

clue.text: Choose randomly from play's actors on a great deal

indicators.note: in a down clue 'on' puts the first piece above the second

parts.note: the cast is the set of actors in a play
lots means a great deal

explanation.surface: Picking a play's cast at random to save a lot of money.
explanation.definitionFit: To cast lots is to decide by drawing tokens, leaving it to chance.

clue.text: Italian resort, resort on high

indicators.note: someone high is intoxicated, so the letters are muddled up

explanation.surface: An Italian resort, a holiday spot up in the hills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'high' looks like altitude but signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Sorrento is a seaside town on the Bay of Naples.

clue.text: Foremost of Spaniards during Iraq tour, dining out — Torquemada, perhaps

indicators.note: with the letters out of place they are rearranged
the foremost letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: Spaniards on a tour of Iraq eat out, led by the infamous Torquemada.
explanation.definitionFit: Tomás de Torquemada was the first Grand Inquisitor of the Spanish Inquisition; 'perhaps' marks an example.

clue.text: Chatter from Hollywood star about principal character in 'Betrayed'

indicators.note: the star's name goes round the next letter

parts.note: Clark Gable was a Hollywood film star

indicators.note: the first letter, the principal character, of the word is taken

explanation.surface: Gossip from a Hollywood star about the lead role in a film called Betrayed.
explanation.definitionFit: To gabble is to talk rapidly and unintelligibly, a kind of chatter.

clue.text: Determined old magistrate imprisoning leader of gang, and daughter

indicators.note: the magistrate holds the next letter inside

parts.note: the Doge was the chief magistrate of old Venice and Genoa

indicators.note: the leading letter of the word

explanation.surface: A resolute old judge jailing a gang boss and his daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: Dogged means tenacious, stubbornly persistent.

clue.text: Not fairly matched in fun event

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the words fun event

explanation.surface: A one-sided contest at a fun event.
explanation.definitionFit: Uneven describes a contest where the sides are unequal.

clue.text: Headdress, first-class, shown in painting put up

indicators.note: in a down clue, put up means read upwards, so backwards
the first-class letters are placed inside

parts.note: painting is art
A1 means first-class, written AI

explanation.surface: A first-class headdress shown in a painting hung on the wall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shown in' gives ARAIT; 'put up' reads it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiara is a jewelled ornamental band worn on the head.

clue.text: Sweetheart gets upset about ending in adventure novel

parts.note: a beau is a boyfriend or sweetheart

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters are disturbed
the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A lover is upset about how an adventure novel ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' joins the upset letters of GETS with the E, which together give GESTE; 'adventure' looks part of the definition but only lends its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Beau Geste is P. C. Wren's 1924 book about the French Foreign Legion.

clue.text: Permission to depart

explanation.surface: Permission to depart.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a noun for authorised absence and a verb meaning to go.

clue.text: Draw large aquatic mammal close to quay

parts.note: an otter is an aquatic mammal

indicators.note: the close, or final letter, of the word

explanation.surface: A sketch of a big otter near the quay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Draw' looks like a verb but is a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A lottery is a draw for prizes by chance.

clue.text: Remove another carat

parts.note: an extra is one more, another
CT is the abbreviation for carat

explanation.surface: A jeweller takes out one more carat.
explanation.definitionFit: To extract is to pull out or take away.
